prompt: Which statement defines the mass of a body in Cambridge International AS Level Physics?
options: the property of a body that resists changes in motion
the gravitational force exerted on a body by the Earth
the product of the volume and weight of a body
the force required to maintain a constant velocity

answer.explanation: Mass is defined as the property of a body that resists changes in motion (inertia).

distractor_explanations: Option 1 is correct. Mass is defined as the property of a body that resists changes in motion.
Option 2 defines weight (a gravitational force), not mass.
Option 3 is dimensionally incorrect and confuses mass with density or weight.
Option 4 reflects the misconception that force is needed to sustain motion; at constant velocity the resultant force is zero.
hints: Recall the controlled definition of mass from the syllabus.
Mass is associated with inertia, the reluctance of an object to accelerate.
solution: Mass is the property of a body that resists changes in motion. Option A is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Begin by defining mass as inertia: it resists changes in velocity (acceleration), not motion itself.
Distinguish mass (a scalar property of matter in kg) from weight (a gravitational vector force in N).
Conclude that option A is the exact syllabus definition.
